commit.message:
docs: add release notes for #11629

In this commit, we add the release note for the subscription fix.

invoices: skip live events already in the subscription backlog

In this commit, we fix a duplicate delivery to new all-invoice
subscribers. SubscribeNotifications registers the client for live events
before it reads the backlog, but deliverBacklogEvents never advanced the
add and settle index of the client. An invoice settled in that window is
committed before the backlog read and also dispatched live, so the
client received it twice.

We now advance the client indices to the last delivered backlog events,
and have dispatchToClients wait for the backlog to finish before it
checks them. The wait also orders the index writes of the subscribing
goroutine before the reads of the event loop.

commit.message:
kvdb/sqlbase: share the connection limit across postgres pools

In this commit, we make the maxConnections limit of dbConnSet a budget
shared by every pgx pool in the set instead of a limit applied to each
pool on its own. Previously, each distinct DSN got its own pool capped
at maxConnections, so N pools could open N times that many connections
and exceed the server's max_connections. The kvdb_postgres tests hit
this because every GetTestBackend call uses a new DSN, which made them
fail with connection errors in CI.

The set now records the driver of each pool. It divides the budget
evenly among the pgx pools and recomputes each one's SetMaxOpenConns
whenever a pool is added or removed, so their limits never add up to
more than the budget. Only pools that talk to one server share a real
limit. Pools of other drivers, such as the per-file SQLite databases,
keep the full limit exactly as before. With a single postgres DSN,
which is what lnd uses outside of tests, the one pool still gets the
full limit.

The postgres test fixture now leaves headroom between the shared budget
and the server's max_connections for the short-lived admin connections
used to create databases, and Dump closes the connection pool it opens.

We add a unit test that checks the pgx limits sum to at most the budget
as pools come and go, that other drivers keep the full limit, and that
the two do not affect each other. We also add a postgres test that runs
a burst of concurrent transactions across many databases. The latter
fails without the change and passes with it.

invoices: add test for duplicate delivery during backlog read

In this commit, we add a test that settles an invoice while a new
all-invoice subscription is held between registering for live events and
reading its backlog. The settle index is committed before the backlog
query runs and the settle is also dispatched live, so the subscriber
receives the invoice twice. The test currently fails because of that
duplicate.

The test uses the existing fault-injecting invoice DB wrapper, extended
with a hook that runs before InvoicesSettledSince, to force the
interleaving deterministically.

lntest/unittest: start bitcoind conn after it syncs to the miner

In this commit, we fix a flake in TestFilteredChainView's bitcoind
polling subtests. NewBitcoindBackend used to start the chain connection
before bitcoind had synced to the miner. In RPC polling mode the
connection polls from bitcoind's height at start (0), so it replays
every historical block afterwards. Under load the replay can still be
running when the chain view registers its client. The replay of the old
tip (equal to the client's best block) is treated as a reorg, which
queues a disconnected event ahead of the connected events. The block
event queue is strictly ordered and nothing reads DisconnectedBlocks
in these tests, so the queue stalls and the filtered block never
arrives.

We now wait for the bitcoind RPC to be reachable, connect it to the
miner and sync, and only then create and start the connection, so the
poller starts at the synced tip and there is nothing to replay.

funding: fix flaky TestFundingManager{CustomChannelParameters,MaxPendingChannels}

In this commit, we fix two independent races in the funding manager
test harness that made these tests fail in CI.

TestFundingManagerCustomChannelParameters read Bob's initial forwarding
policy as soon as it had received his FundingSigned message. Bob sends
that message before he stores the policy, so the read could return
"channel not found". Bob emits the pending open event only after the
policy is stored, so the test now waits for that event first.

TestFundingManagerMaxPendingChannels has several channels waiting on
confirmation at once, but the mock notifier handed every registration
the same one-conf channel. Whichever goroutine received a confirmation
was arbitrary, so it could get the confirmation carrying another
channel's funding tx, fail validation, and never send ChannelReady. The
mock notifier can now route one-conf registrations by funding txid, and
this test confirms each tx on its own channel. Other tests keep the
shared channel.

commit.message:
pool: fix flaky TestConcreteRecyclePoolTests

In this commit, we fix a flake in testRecyclePool, which failed with
"original item not found" on a loaded CI runner.

GCQueue.Take hands out a freshly allocated item when the queue manager
goroutine does not answer within one millisecond. The test allowed only
two takes, so a single stalled take (common under -race or -cover with
parallel packages) used up an attempt without consuming the queued
original, and the test gave up even though the returned item was still
in the queue.

The pool only promises best-effort reuse, so we now take until the
original item is delivered. A timed-out take does not remove anything
from the queue, so the original is always reached. We also use gc and
expiry intervals of a minute so that the original cannot expire while
the test runs, and drop the one millisecond sleep that only masked the
scheduling dependence. The cleanliness assertion on the original is
unchanged.

commit.message:
tor: don't resolve a direct connection's address through Tor

In this commit, we make Dial skip ParseAddr for a connection that went
around the proxy because of SkipProxyForClearNetTargets.

After connecting directly to a clearnet hostname, Dial still resolved
that hostname through Tor to fill in the connection's remote address.
With Tor down or unable to resolve the name, a dial that had already
succeeded then failed, and the connection was left open. A direct
connection already reports the peer's own address, so we now return it
as is. dialProxy reports whether it skipped the proxy, so the rule
stays in one place, and Dial closes the connection if ParseAddr fails.

We also make the onion assertions in the lookup test check that the
error comes from the proxy, as the system resolver fails on an onion
host as well, so they'd pass even if onion hosts weren't proxied.
